fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Circular Driveway; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Circular Driveway; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the roadway.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to make the access point visible at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the full width of the long access drive clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so emergency vehicles can reach the residence without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain adequate vehicle clearance for fire apparatus and ambulances.
• Mark the circular driveway surface or curb edges with reflective indicators so responders unfamiliar with the property can identify the vehicle path after dark.
• Keep the circular driveway free of parked vehicles, trailers, or stored equipment so arriving apparatus can complete the turn and stage near the residence.
• Post a diagram of the property layout, including the location of the detached structures and the circular driveway, at the road entrance so responders can orient quickly before committing vehicles down the long drive.
• Identify and mark a secondary turnaround point along the access drive in case the circular driveway is blocked, so large vehicles have a known option for reversing.
• Keep gates, if any exist along the access drive, unlocked or equipped with a Knox lock so responders are not delayed at a single access point.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Long Driveway; Vegetation Along Driveway; Mixed Vegetation; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin trees in clusters near the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and ground vegetation growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Clear a wide band of low vegetation around the entire perimeter of the house to separate it from the surrounding plant material.
• Cut back or remove shrubs and low-hanging branches along both sides of the driveway for its full length.
• Trim tree branches that overhang the driveway to keep the travel lane clear for vehicles.
• Remove dead grass, leaves, and plant debris that have collected against or under the structure.
• Thin scattered trees along the driveway to reduce the amount of vegetation lining the access route.
• Keep the ground beneath trees near the house clear of dead leaves, needles, and loose plant material.
• Remove shrubs growing between trees near the structure to break up connected patches of vegetation.
• Maintain clear sight lines along the driveway so the structure is visible from the road.
• Keep the single access route free of fallen branches and overgrown vegetation that could block a vehicle.
• Mow or cut ground vegetation in open areas close to the structure to reduce the amount of low-lying plant material near it.
